report.summary: The only failure is test_invalid_book_is_rejected[blank-title], which expects a whitespace-only title to get 422 but gets 201. The app's title check in validate_book (app/main.py:75) uses `if not book.title`, which does not strip whitespace, so "   " is accepted; the author check on line 77 does strip. Fix the product code first by changing line 75 to `if not book.title.strip():`, then add a UI or API case for a whitespace-only title.

causes.title: Whitespace-only book title is accepted instead of rejected with 422
causes.explanation: validate_book checks the title with `if not book.title:`, which is only true for an empty string. A title of three spaces is truthy, so validation passes and insert_book writes the row. The author check directly below uses `book.author.strip()`, so the title check is inconsistent with it and with the test's stated requirement that a blank title is rejected with 'Title must not be blank'. The behavior is deterministic, so the test is right to fail.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:66: assert response.status_code == 422 / E       assert 201 == 422 / +  where 201 = <Response [201 Created]>.status_code
test parameter: book = {'title': '   ', 'author': 'A'}, message = 'Title must not be blank'
app/main.py:153-158: insert_book calls validate_book(book) and then INSERTs book.title unchanged
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py:75 change `if not book.title:` to `if not book.title.strip():`. Optionally strip the stored title as well so that padded titles are saved consistently. Re-run tests/api/test_books_api.py to confirm the blank-title case passes.
